People who would like to verify it locally can clone the 4.0.2 repo, (I assume one has rust and docker installed) 

**Install srtool: **
cargo install --git https://github.com/chevdor/srtool-cli

srtool build --root --package edgeware-runtime --runtime-dir node/runtime .

We would like to add some specific notes that could be of use to validators for this upgrade. It would be ideal to put those as part of the communication that notify them to upgrade the new client.
1. The wasm upgrade can take a long time to complete: it takes ~30secs on the testnet but could really be significantly longer with many validators. If any part of your stack involves some kind of uptime-check monitoring tool with small threshold, you may want to disable it or allow for a bigger leeway around the upgrade time. We could remain a full minute or more without a block while the upgrade is being processed and you need to plan accordingly.
2. On block 14555555 and independently from the runtime upgrade, there will be a consensus modification in Aura that will affect only the end of eras. At the end of the era where consensus change happens (the one that block 14555555 belongs to), the authorities will not change at the turn block, but at the next block. For instance, in our current consensus, if the new era is at block #100 and there is a change of authorities (the list of validators change because new ones enter and old ones are excluded), at block 99 and the new ones are producing block #100. After, the old authorities are signing block #100 and the new ones only start signing from block #101. This is because of [this old change in substrate](https://github.com/paritytech/substrate/pull/9132) that modified the consensus so we are switching from the legacy behaviour to what's consistent with substrate today. This means that one validator will do one more turn that usual. This could cause issues if for instance your stack uses scripts that rely on strict blocks to perform operations at the end of each era so it could be necessary to add some tolerance, or to modify them so that they behave differently before and after block 14555555. 
3. ParityDB has graduated from unsafe to safe and can now be used. This has become the preferred one in Polkadot, although rocksDB is still fully supported. You can use either of them and both seem to sync and perform correctly from our tests. One thing to note is that switching databases from one to another requires a full re-sync. Also the new client converts the database format so that it will not be possible to downgrade without resyncing (at least we observed that behaviour with rocksDB)

full_text:
[Could eventually post through CW.im but not through gov.edgewa.re it seems the selector is even more broken. Can we get back to the old version which was ugly but not as bad as that one?]

Reposted from the proposals matrix channels:

I wanted to give an update on the upcoming release. This got delayed a bit abruptly last week due to our validator KDPNETSTAKE triggering a critical consensus bug on the testnet (BTW run totally voluntarily by our validator JelliedOwl (Paul) ), not only they got this triggered, but they kept the state long enough for me to extract information about what the issue was, so they should be warmly thanked because they prevented really nasty issue to happen.

I don't think it's the place to enter into the technical details of the issue, but the short story is that there had been a consensus change in Aura - the block production method we use in Edgeware - about 2 years ago, triggered by other changes within substrate and nobody noticed at the time. We are on an older version, so it did not affect us. I found out and pointed this issue almost one year ago but at the time, I though it could be fixed easily outside of substrate, but there were some cases that were still an issue.
The main challenges in solving this were about not doing too many incremental upgrades and not having to fork our own version of substrate and maintain this till the end of times. And I think this is done now... with some caveats.

The main take is that we will need to change the consensus too to be in line with substrate in the future and get rid of all the specific transition code that's now in the updated client that we will ask the validators to run. For now I have hardcoded this to happen at block 14555555, so in a bit less than one month at a half.

It has consequences on the vote and also on validators expected behaviour. We expect to get approval for the runtime upgrade BEFORE that block ideally. Here is why: we will ask validators to upgrade their clients, then trigger a vote once a vast majority has performed it, and if succcessful, the runtime upgrade will naturally exclude potential validators running the old client, since they won't be able to participate in the new consensus. This is the "clean" way of filtering them. Then at block 14555555, the consensus will change and there will be no issue since all validators remaining are guaranteed to be on the new client.
Now, if the upgrade does not get through, but all validators upgraded their client, we have no issue either: everyone will get it's consensus change at the block trigger.
The problem is if the upgrade does not get through, AND not all validators have upgraded by block 14555555, the COULD be some problems in case the authority set changes, where part of the validators would see some blocks to be valid, some would see them invalid. If more than 2/3 of the validators have upgraded by the time, we will like miss blocks, but we can stay in consensus. The chain would get slower to process blocks, but it would follow on (same if less than 1/3 of the validators have upgraded, but that would really be a disastrous scenario since we would remain with the same logic no upgrade, no consensus change, old substrate from 2 years ago), but in case the proportion of upgrade/not upgraded is close to the same, we would have a total disagreement on which block is valid and which one isn't and the chain would never finalize. Worse, in case a majority of validators change in an era, the chain would just stop.
The risk of this to happen is very low, but this is why we really expect the upgrade approved before. All upgrades have their fair share of risk anyway, and especially that one that's migrating us from substrate 2 to substrate 4.

I would like to talk about a timing proposal as I see it: we will have a ~2 weeks testnet and then we will trigger the vote. The whole voting process, enactment etc. take about 10 days so we should be upgraded in 3.5 weeks and the consensus change triggered around 2 weeks afterwards.

Also, we have really a lack of waiting validators right now and it is possible that we lose more of them with the upgrade, because some may just not feel like it's worth their time to upgrade the client. Additionally I am myself currently running more validators than I am comfortable with, so we will try to monitor who has upgraded and get a rough assessment of the number of new clients. And we will propose a vote to reduce the number of validators JUST before the upgrade. Note that I have unbonded a lot of mine, so that the first ones to be excluded from the set would be mine, but depending on how many upgraded, we could need to reduce more. This is to prevent the chain to stop finalizing in case less than 2/3 upgraded. Of course, we can have a vote immediately after the upgrade to bring it back to a higher number if we have valid waiting validators.

Hope this is mostly clear for everybody. Please ping me out if you feel any of this can cause issues.
